questions.q: What information does a bag-of-words representation discard?
options: The word counts
The vocabulary
Word order, so 'dog bites man' and 'man bites dog' look identical
The number of documents
questions.explain: Bag-of-words keeps how often each word appears but not where. N-grams recover a little local order at the cost of a bigger vocabulary.

questions.q: In the lesson's four-review corpus, 'died' (in 1 of 4 documents) got a higher IDF than 'day' (in 3 of 4). What does that mean?
options: Rarer words receive larger IDF weights, so they count for more in TF-IDF
Words that appear in more documents always get larger weights
IDF measures how many letters a word has
The vectorizer made an error because 'day' is a real word
questions.explain: Inverse document frequency rewards words that appear in few documents, since they are more distinctive.

questions.q: Why should a TfidfVectorizer be fit on the training data only?
options: Because fitting on test data is slower
Because scikit-learn refuses to transform unseen documents
Because vectorizers can only learn from fewer than 100 documents
Because fitting on all the data leaks test vocabulary and document frequencies into training
questions.explain: Vocabulary and IDF are learned from data. Learning them from the test set leaks information; fit on training data, then transform the test set.

questions.q: What happens to a word in a new sentence that was never seen when the vectorizer was fit, such as 'the' in the lesson's example?
options: It raises an error
It is ignored, because it has no column in the vocabulary
It is added to the vocabulary automatically
It receives the highest possible weight
questions.explain: transform only produces columns for words in the fitted vocabulary, so unseen words contribute nothing.

questions.q: Why is the output of CountVectorizer stored as a sparse matrix?
options: Sparse matrices are more accurate than dense arrays
Only sparse matrices can be passed to classifiers
Most cells are zero (63% even in the tiny example), so storing only non-zero cells saves large amounts of memory
It makes the vocabulary smaller
questions.explain: A real vocabulary has tens of thousands of columns and each document uses few of them, so a sparse format stores only the non-zero entries.
